doc.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002

title: The house, the 1991 fire and Charlie Parker Place
summary: Jordan bought the land about 1981; the old house burned in 1991 but the pictures were saved, and her lawn bears a Charlie Parker Place street sign.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I moved here, I bought this land about 1981. There was an old house that sits in front of this one, it was 150 years old, and I was out on tour in Canada and had just finished renovating it in 1991, ten years later, and it burned to the ground. And I was like in shock. But nobody was hurt. And all of my pictures were saved so that was an amazing kind of thing, that all the pictures, the things that really meant a lot, most all pictures of just everybody you know, and so that was a good thing, that I got the pictures. And then this house, I moved it back a little further from the road and I’ve been very happy here. It’s a little bit more comfortable for me in the sense that it’s not thirteen rooms. I don’t know, my idea of when I even bought the place was, as you saw my lawn, it’s called Charlie Parker Place. And I got that sign, a street sign from a festival that they did on his birthday, the first festival they did when they named a street in New York City after Bird. Charlie Parker Place. And I did the first concert, actually the first two concerts. And they gave me that street sign. And I said well I don’t know if I’ll ever get the money together to have a workshop up this way but we can dream, we’ve gotta dream. So I called it Charlie Parker Place.
